leading_positions.synthesis: Six of the eight round-1 files explicitly prefer a single-part prize for B013 to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. Shared: the prediction of the Z2 quantum spin Hall state, its first observation in HgTe quantum wells, and about eighteen years of independent confirmation by transport and photoemission. Not shared: citation wording. Some versions end on the first experimental observation in HgTe wells, while others (Danielsson, Olsson) end on establishing topological insulators as a new class of matter, which is broader and edges toward the 3D branch. Danielsson reports that Eriksson would swap Mele for Hasan, but Eriksson's own configuration keeps Mele, and Danielsson himself would keep Mele. Every supporter lists Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan as omissions. Danielsson moved to B013 from B008, Johansson from B009 and Pearce from B008, so part of the convergence follows from the opening round.

Kroll alone prefers a prize to Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks, arguing that the two-name attribution is unusually clean and that the clocks are reproduced at several institutes at the 10^-18 level. His own reservations are that this may be read as a metrology instrument rather than a discovery, that the redefinition of the second is pending, and that it follows the frequency-comb prize of 2005. He ranked B013 low in the openings because it is outside his field, not because he judged it weak, and he names B013 as his first alternative. His position is an explicit minority view and not a rejection of B013.

Lindroth alone prefers a prize to Bloch, Greiner and Zoller for ultracold atoms in optical lattices, built around the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and quantum gas microscopes. She treats it as a discovery about many-body matter and not only a platform. Her own concerns are a five-name credited set squeezed into three seats (Esslinger, Cirac and the uncredited Jaksch), possible diffuseness of the citation, and a possible bias from being the member closest to atomic physics. She lists B013 as her first alternative.

areas_of_agreement: No member contests the physics of B013: the Z2 classification with protected edge states and the HgTe observation of quantised edge conduction are treated as a prediction followed by a clean, independently reproduced experiment.

Six of eight explicit preferred configurations are the identical trio Kane, Mele and Molenkamp under B013, and Kroll and Lindroth each name B013 as their first listed alternative. No file argues that B013 should not be awarded.

Every member who writes on B013 names the same three problems: the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal lies outside the credited names (Zhang is deceased), Hasan's 3D ARPES work is left out by a trio, and the 2016 topological-phases prize requires a clear statement of what is distinct.
No member's disclosed conflict affects B013, and no one has asked to recuse from it.
Maturity is not the obstacle for B013. Several members cite roughly eighteen years of independent confirmation, and the doubts about maturity are directed at other candidates (B021, B025).
scientific_disputes: Whether a second topology prize after 2016 is a distinct recognition. Supporters say symmetry-protected band topology in real materials differs from topological phase transitions and Hall-type phases, but Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce all flag the question and none claims it is settled.

Whether the right scope of B013 is the 2D quantum spin Hall effect alone or topological insulators as a class including the 3D materials. The citations proposed differ here, and this affects whether the trio is a complete story.

Whether optical lattice clocks (Kroll's B006) are a discovery or a measurement tool. Lindroth reads them as a technical advance. Kroll answers with the capability they open: relativistic geodesy, constant-drift limits and dark-matter searches.
Whether cold-atom quantum simulation (Lindroth's B002) is a discovery about emergent many-body physics or an enabling platform, which determines whether its citation can be precise.

Whether circuit QED (B009) adds anything physically new beyond the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits. Danielsson and Johansson both raise this, and Johansson now gives his own first opening choice less weight.
attribution_disputes: B013 has four credited names for three seats. Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce keep Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, while Eriksson is reported in Danielsson's reply as having raised swapping Mele for Hasan. Danielsson replies that Kane and Mele are a single theory contribution that cannot be split. Olsson and Kroll also ask whether Hasan should substitute for Mele. Nobody has proposed dropping Molenkamp.

Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are outside the credited names but are described as the ones who told Molenkamp where to look. Zhang's death removes one possible laureate. Several members ask whether a citation can be accurate about each person's contribution without them.
B002 has five credited names (Bloch, Cirac, Greiner, Zoller, Esslinger) for Lindroth's trio of Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, and Zoller's theory is tied to Jaksch, who is not credited.

B006 omits ion-clock pioneers and the Ludlow, Hinkley and Bloom generation, and Kroll has not verified priority between Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and parallel lattice-clock work around 2003 to 2005.

B008 is credited to one name (Halzen) for a very large collaboration and earlier pioneers (AMANDA, Baikal, ANTARES). Danielsson, Olsson and I all note this, and it is why Danielsson and I, who each ranked it first in our openings, now hold it as an alternative.
maturity_disputes: B021 (fractional charge and anyonic statistics): Danielsson and Mehlig regard fractional charge by shot noise as secure but the anyonic braiding evidence as only a few years old, and want more independent replication or an outside report.

B025 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene): Johansson notes that the pairing mechanism may be clearer within a few years, which would change the maturity assessment. Olsson asks whether Andrei's earlier STM flat-band observation should displace one of the credited trio.
B006: Kroll accepts that the impact case is partly prospective until the redefinition of the second takes place.
B013 is the only candidate on which no file raises a maturity objection.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology at Chalmers, works closely with superconducting-circuit groups, and ranked B009 first in his opening. He asks that his views on B009 be treated with caution and says he would consider recusing himself from decisions that depend mainly on it. He reports no conflict for B013, B025 or the other shortlisted entries.

Pearce (chair): astroparticle background and PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations. No credited person in B013, B025 or B008 is a known collaborator, but he cannot be fully neutral on B008 and is outside his expertise on condensed matter.

Kroll notes an institutional overlap with Johansson through the Chalmers-led WACQT, relevant to B009 but not to his preferred B006. His rare-earth quantum-memory work and company interests are not connected to any shortlisted candidate.
Lindroth: close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and of the Lund and ETH attosecond groups. She reports no specific conflict for B002, B013 or B022.
Olsson: notes a Chalmers colleague link to Johansson and membership of the materials-characterisation community, with no known tie to Andrei (B025). No conflict is reported for B013.
questions_for_round2: For B013, will the committee settle on Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, or does any member argue for Hasan in place of one of them? If so, which of the three would be replaced, and on what basis of priority and decisiveness?

How should the B013 citation treat the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the 3D topological insulator work, given that neither is among the three laureates? Should the wording be limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall effect, or can it say topological insulators as a class without overclaiming for the three named people?

Can the committee state in one sentence why B013 is distinct from the 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions? Will those members who raised the objection (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) accept that sentence as sufficient?

Kroll and Lindroth rank B013 as their first alternative, so should the final configuration be a single part? Would either accept B013 alone, and if not, which of B006 and B002, and with how many named people, would they put forward as a second part or an alternative?

For B006 and B002, can the credited names be reduced to workable laureate sets (Katori and Ye for B006; three of Bloch, Greiner, Zoller, Esslinger and Cirac for B002), and what is the position on the omitted names (Jaksch, ion-clock pioneers)?

Johansson, with respect to B009: does he recuse from discussion of it, or only from the vote? Danielsson and Johansson also raised the overlap with the 2025 prize. What is the specific physics in circuit QED that the 2025 citation did not cover?

What is the standard for B008, since I and others see the single-name credit as a barrier? Is any supported configuration with more than one laureate available from the supplied names, or does B008 stay as an alternative only?
summary.chair_observation: The round-1 files show one clear convergence and two single-member minority positions. Six members explicitly prefer the same B013 trio and the other two name B013 as their first alternative, so what remains is allocation and wording, not whether the field merits recognition. The risks stated in the files are that the trio omits Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, and that a second topology prize after 2016 must be justified in plain terms. The minority positions (B006, B002) are argued on merit and carry their own attribution and discovery-versus-tool questions that round 2 should address directly. Convergence in this round follows in part from members reading each other's openings, which the committee should bear in mind when weighing it.
